about: Stage 7's data (tools/body/correctives.py). keys: [motion, absolute deg] posed as the check poses them (bends.Strip; hip_abd: the hip turned about her front). Regions: spheres round the joint's rest head, full within r_in, none past r_out (m). pull: the reference curves (tools/body/ref) the outline is pulled to (the joint's own anatomy: olecranon, patella plane, deltoid cap, folds); cap: the farthest an outline point is pulled (m); outline: that term's weight multiplier. Elbow keys within 8 deg of the rest angle (MakeHuman's 39.7) are dropped: a 45 key there would be a null shape. v1 (4 Nov): the shoulder's solve is held back (it lost area and outline against LBS: see the P1 report), as are knee 135 and hip 135 (the last key holds past it). The hip's shapes are held back too (hip_abd45 solved a 143 mm shape; the right hip at 90 read 52 inside against the left's 12: the midline mirror is not yet right).

joints.name: elbow
joints.why: P1 D (5 Nov), on OUR topology and weights v1 (wide crease band, 4b off). Keys 90 and 135 only: the 5 key (straightening from her 40.4 rest) is dropped, LBS there already holds (inside 0, girth .99-1.05, area .98-1.09), so below the rest the law holds the null. side 'geom': each node's side of the plane by the REST bisector plane (the check's seg_d), not the 0.5 distal weight: with the wide band the 0.5 line sits off the crease and the fold pinned 286 rounded-corner nodes to the wrong side (175 inside at 90 against LBS's 0). 90: the inner and outer curves pulled (cap 30 mm: the inner corner sits up to 27 px off, the sharpening the wide band needs), no pressure. 135: pressure, the section swell as a push along the skin normal (the edge-scaling swell grew girth to 1.2 for area .79: scaling stretches the skin round a pinned face), restoring the rest area per station to p 1.0 / d 0.88 of the rest (the forearm's girth is the bound: d 0.94 pushed d0.1 to 1.09), faded to none within 10 mm of the contact (the corner's normals converge: pushing there folded the skin, 11 inside); clamp: the plane as a hard wall after the last round.

joints.name: knee
joints.why: P1 D (5 Nov), on OUR topology and weights v1. The flatten fold (crease_fold.py) now, not v1's 'plane' solve; keys 90 and 135 (the 45 key dropped: LBS holds there and the 90 key's hat starts at the rest 4.8). side 'geom' as the elbow's. 90: LBS has no crossing but the back of the knee caves to the joint (the inner outline 35 px off the reference corner); the inner and outer curves pulled (cap 30 mm), the contact held through the reference's inner corner, not the joint (corner_shift: a thin back of the thigh against a full calf puts the corner 13 mm toward the thigh; a fold held on the joint's plane dented the crease there), the shift eased in over 20 mm from the joint's axis (a full shift at the axis drove the thigh's skin into the calf beside the joint: 11 inside), margin 0.5 mm (1.5 mm left a 3 mm see-through slit 18 mm deep in the side view) and the contact sagged 1.5 mm at 5 cm across the limb (bow -0.6/m: a flat contact seen edge-on still shows its 1 mm gap as a slit, 19 px; a soft contact is not flat). 135: the elbow's pressure (p 1.0, d 0.88), the outer curve only.

joints.name: hip
joints.why: P1 hip r2 (5 Nov): HELD (no hip shape ships). On the r2 weights (the perineum pin, the trunk side) raw skinning passes hip 90 but for the front pit: 0 inside, girth 1.057 (the geometric selection), pits F7.3 S1.9 B6.9 M7.5 mm; this 90 key, re-solved on them, made the judge's side pit back (S 1.9 -> 7.0, F 8.2, M 14.6) while 0 inside, so it is held; its spillover helped 112 (no key 386 inside / 44 mm, key 173 / 31) and not 135 (644 / 66 either way). 112-135 need the two-body contact (pair_trial below: contact_pair.py, fold 'pair', law 'arc', keys 90-135, not shipped: at 105 it leaves ~90 belly nodes inside although each sits on the thigh's surface + 0.8 mm, so the gap itself tests inside: the draped belly does not yet separate the two bodies; cause open). Earlier: P1 D (5 Nov), SHORT of the acceptance (see the P1 D report). Key flex 90 only, by direction (rbf over the thigh's direction in the pelvis frame, sigma 40: the rest key no shape, so 0 at rest). The hinge's flatten fold does not carry to the hip: the bisector plane through the joint (8-10 cm behind the groin) cut the belly, through the reference corner it still flattened the whole lower trunk across the midline (180 inside), so the pairwise contact (solve_key: the rigid parts' signed distances + ray parity) with the strip's body only (free_rend: the other leg and the arms are held as posed), the inner and outer curves pulled, and the midline held to the pelvis within 4 cm (hold_mid: LBS swings the perineum's left half with the left thigh through the right half; held, its depth fell 87 -> 24 mm). Flex 135 is held back: the thigh meets the belly there (652 inside under LBS) and this solve left 502 with girth 1.13; it needs a two-body contact solve, not a hinge fold. D2 (5 Nov): the rebuild the D verdict asks for (contact_fold.py, fold 'stepped', law 'arc') was tried and is NOT shipped: its trial settings are kept under 'd2_trial' (held). Findings: the smooth-skin ARAP over a 25 cm sphere drifts off the skeleton's pivot (p95 4.9 mm, -75 cm3 at 7.5 deg flexion, no contact; the rest-umbrella and full-matrix Laplacian targets the same: 12.7 mm p95 at 45 deg), so the correction must be U = Y - X on the skinned surface (min |L U|^2 + an anchor >= 0.3: a 0.0016 anchor spread one 2 cm push over 10+ cm, +372 cm3); a rigid capped thigh solid as the obstacle pushes the buttock (behind) and the root's blend, and the posed-surface contacts leave 220 points at ~100 mm (check depth) at 135 against LBS's 652 at 75 mm: neither beats D's 90 key (14 at 24 mm). The 15 deg in-between keys need the 'arc' law (rig_drive.py): the Gaussian rbf rings with dense keys (5 keys 15 deg apart summed to 2.0 at 45).

joints.name: shoulder
joints.why: P1 D (5 Nov): held (no shapes). On weights v1 with the girdle helpers, LBS already meets the shoulder acceptance (abd 90/135 inside 0/7 at 0 mm, girth <= 1.006; flex 90/135 inside 0/0 left, 0/2 right, girth <= 0.999) and this solve regressed it: girth to 1.08-1.10 at abd 90 and flex 90, 91 inside at flex 135 (the ARAP's blended rotations on the helper-driven girdle). The rbf law (rig_drive.py) is ready for shapes when a girdle solve beats LBS.
